This is the standing measurement floor for any prose+fenced-bash edit to a Step 10d arm and cannot be tightened without materializing a test harness for the block; the analyzer should note it as a scope caveat if a future partial-apply outcome surfaces.
- **Diff-producer read symmetry (§4 Edit A, assumption A6).** `git diff --name-only HEAD "issue-<N>" -- <paths>` reads from the SAME ref the `git checkout issue-<N> -- <paths>` above WROTE FROM. Per A6 any divergence at this diff is by construction a partial apply. This closes the "wrong-source" class but not the class where `/tmp/issue-<N>-additive-files.txt` itself is truncated or reordered between the checkout and the diff read (both consume the same file, so a truncation is symmetric and reads clean). Minor: the terminal `false` still routes to `partial-apply-verify-failed`, so no false `landed` slips through; but a debug read of the sentinel outcome would be more informative if stderr were captured to `/tmp/issue-<N>-postapply-stderr.txt`.

## CRITIC REPORT: Task #1694 workflow-fix plan v1 (Methodology)

**Rating: REVISE**

### Must Fix (conclusion-changing only)

1. **Edit A's terminal `false` does NOT prevent the subsequent push from
   overwriting the sentinel.** The plan inserts a diff-verify fence between
   the `git commit` (SKILL.md line 11862) and the `if timeout ... git push
   origin main; then echo landed > ... fi` (lines 11871-11876). SKILL.md is
   not run under `set -e` (grepped: no `set -e` anywhere in the file), so a
   plain `false` at the end of an `if`/`elif` branch sets exit code but does
   NOT short-circuit the surrounding block. Concretely: verify fails →
   sentinel `partial-apply` written → `false` → **the immediately-following
   `if timeout … git push origin main; then echo landed >
   /tmp/issue-<N>-surgical-outcome.txt` runs, and on push success the
   `landed` write overwrites `partial-apply`.** The plan's own claim ("push
   proceeds only when the fence exits 0") is not what the code does — it is
   what the code would do under `set -e`, which is not the surrounding
   contract. This directly regresses the fail-fast property Edit A was
   supposed to introduce (CLAUDE.md § Critical Rules: "Fail fast — never hide
   failures"): a partial apply would still land the `landed` sentinel, the
   `epm:merged v1` marker would still post, and the 3c24493113-class
   incident recurs unchanged.

   Fix: wrap the push in a conditional gated on the verify's result. Two
   correct shapes:
   (a) capture the verify's exit code into a shell variable, THEN branch
   ("`APPLY_OK=1; if ! git ... ; then APPLY_OK=0; echo … partial-apply ... ;
   elif [ -s … ]; then APPLY_OK=0; echo … partial-apply … ; fi; if [
   "$APPLY_OK" = 1 ]; then if timeout … git push origin main; then echo
   landed … else echo push-failed … false; fi; fi`"), or
   (b) short-circuit with early `return`/`exit` in the failure arms — but
   the block is a bash-fenced snippet inside a background call, so `exit`
   would kill the wrapping shell rather than route through the
   completion-read sentinel, and `return` is not valid outside a function.
   (a) is the drop-in.
   The `if timeout ... git push … then echo landed … else echo push-failed
   … false; fi` currently on lines 11871-11876 MUST move inside the new
   apply-ok arm. — grounding: plan §4 Design "Insert this fence, as a NEW
   step inside the existing `if [ "$GATE_VERDICT" = "pass" ]; then` arm —
   between the `git commit` and the `if timeout ... git push`
   bounded-push"; SKILL.md lines 11862, 11871-11876. — mechanizable: yes —
   a code-reviewer running `grep -B2 -A15 'PARTIAL-APPLY VERIFY' … SKILL.md`
   asserts the push block is REACHABLE only from the apply-ok arm (the `if
   timeout … git push` line MUST be preceded by an `if [ "$APPLY_OK" … ]; then`
   or equivalent gate, not just fall through from the fence).

### What's Good About This Plan

The design correctly identifies the two real defects (silent-partial-apply
in the surgical-checkout arm; guard exiting nonzero on every routine infra
task). It scopes both edits to fenced-bash blocks that follow the existing
materialize-then-check discipline of the surrounding code (Guard-1's own
`ls-tree` producer, the pre-push lint-gate's `comm -23` subtraction) —
these patterns match the block's style. Edit B is well-conceived: the
unconditional pre-sync + falling-back to the existing #1300 pre-check as a
backstop is the right ordering (single-flight flock semantics make repeat
calls safe; the existing pre-check remains as documented defense-in-depth).
The recurrence-pattern audit in §4 correctly concludes only the surgical
checkout commit asserts an unverified state (the other `git commit -m`
sites — spec-freshness, agent-memory, guard-1 strip, methodology,
merge-conflict `--no-edit`, post-merge stale-folder removal — either
commit mechanical git-native results or commit deterministic file
operations whose message describes exactly what was done). The `git diff
--name-only HEAD "issue-<N>" -- <paths>` invocation is the correct probe
(it reads exactly the content the wholesale checkout wrote), and the
assumption chain (A1-A6) is well-anchored.

### Concerns the analyzer/reviewer should weigh (NOT blocking)

- **§4 line-number citations are stale in the recurrence-pattern audit.**
  The plan claims "safe-case `gh pr merge $MERGE_FORM` (line ~11134)",
  "Guard-1 strip commit (line ~10009)", "merge-conflict recovery `git
  commit --no-edit` (line ~11475)", and "pre-gate spec-freshness commit
  (line ~7040 area)". Actual line numbers (grepped 2026-07-26): the
  safe-case `gh pr merge $MERGE_FORM` is elsewhere (no `git commit -m`
  literal there — GitHub does the merge server-side); Guard-1 strip is
  line 9900; merge-conflict is line 11374; spec-freshness is line 2280.
  This does not change the audit's SUBSTANTIVE conclusion (only the
  surgical-checkout commit claims something git itself cannot verify —
  correct), just the line-number references are wrong. Non-blocking; the
  implementer will regenerate them from `grep` anyway.

- **Edit A's diff producer scope is subtle when a filename contains
  whitespace or shell-globbing chars.** The plan uses `$(cat
  /tmp/issue-<N>-additive-files.txt)` unquoted inside the diff command,
  which subjects the file list to word-splitting and glob expansion.
  Additive files with spaces / brackets / dollar signs would misfire.
  Present code (`xargs -r -a <file>`) does the equivalent right — the
  implementer should mirror the `xargs` form: e.g. `xargs -r -a
  /tmp/issue-<N>-additive-files.txt git -C "$REPO_ROOT" diff --name-only
  HEAD "issue-<N>" -- > /tmp/… 2>/dev/null || false`. Reviewer-catchable.

- **Edit A's diff comparison direction (`HEAD` vs `issue-<N>`) requires the
  local `issue-<N>` branch ref to exist AND to point at the same tip
  content the checkout READ FROM.** A6 asserts this by construction (the
  block itself reads from `issue-<N>` immediately above), which is
  correct at HEAD-of-plan-authoring — but any future block reorder that
  moves the branch fetch/checkout out of order would silently invalidate
  the fence. Not blocking now; a code-reviewer inspecting Edit A should
  note the ordering assumption.

- **Edit B's `sync_repo_root.py` is single-flight flock — a concurrent
  sync returning exit 0 without our push landing IS documented as the
  fallback case, but the `|| echo "…non-zero…"` catcher only fires on
  non-zero exit.** A concurrent-sync exit 0 (successfully deferred to
  another caller) leaves us pre-guard without our own state pushed —
  which is exactly the state the existing #1300 pre-check is there to
  fall through to and recover. Since Edit B PRESERVES that #1300 arm,
  this is fine, but reviewers should verify the #1300 arm still fires
  when the pre-sync silently deferred.
